definition: Lavish means given without limits — poured out in abundance; as a verb, to give something without limits.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word lavish. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know lavish should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The publisher's lavish anniversary edition ran to three ribbon bookmarks, gilt page edges, and forty new color plates.
Generous is milder than lavish: a generous host gives gladly and amply, while a lavish one pours it out past all keeping track — more courses, more gifts, more everything.
Extravagant goes further than lavish — lavish giving still earns admiring gasps, but extravagant spending has crossed into excess that even the admirers call unwise.

Extravagant means spending or giving beyond what sense allows — the word arrives with a raised eyebrow. Lavish shares the abundance but not the frown: lavish admires the overflowing hand, extravagant audits it.

Unstinting means holding nothing back — giving without stint or limit, usually said of effort, praise, or support. It measures the giver's steadiness; lavish measures the poured-out result you can see on the table.

Lavish describes giving poured past every requirement — not just generous, which credits the spirit of the giver, but overflowing in the visible result: ponies, telescopes, boxes upon boxes of shoes.

Extravagant covers the same overflow with a frown — spending past sense — and generous credits the giver's spirit rather than the size of what lands on the table.
As a verb, lavish takes 'on': grandparents lavish attention on the baby.
